newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian gunmen wound eight, then flee.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian gunmen wound eight, then flee.

text.p: Unidentified gunmen shot and wounded eight people including two policemen in the southern province of Fayoum on Tuesday, the Interior Ministry said.

It said in a statement that Lieutenant Mohamed Fathi Mahmoud was on his way home from the police checkpoint at Kahak village some 100 km (60 miles) south of Cairo when he spotted a car careening down the street without licence plates.
When Mahmoud tried to stop them to investigate, the gunmen sprayed a taxi and passers-by with machinegun fire.
They then escaped and police forces have cordonned off the area to hunt them down, the statement said.
It did not say if the men were members of the Moslem militant groups fighting the government since 1992 but said the car fitted descriptions of others used in "recent incidents".
Last month, gunmen stormed a bank in al-Ayat village almost 50 km (30 miles) south of Cairo, stealing an unspecified amount of money and killing two. They escaped in a waiting car.
Militants sometimes storm gold shops and banks for funding. Almost 1,000 people have been killed in the political violence which has erupted in Egypt.
